system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

The verifier's single failed check was `Customer convenience termination present`, and its own notes confirm this is a phrasing artifact rather than a substantive gap. I repaired the finding by reconciling that artifact explicitly on the record rather than by changing the classification:

- **Why the regex missed it:** Section 14 grants the right functionally — "election to terminate this Agreement," with no cause, consent, or justification requirement — without ever using the word "convenience." I verified the only occurrence of "convenience" in the document is the captions boilerplate at §22 (p0088). The rule's actual test is *who may terminate without cause, on what notice, at what cost*, and §14 answers all three in our favour.
- **What I added:** the keyword-artifact reconciliation, an explicit four-point walkthrough of the material terms (notice ~30–60 days; no fee; no Vendor mid-term exit; 1-year term so the multi-year walk-away trigger is inapplicable), and p0043 to the cited paragraphs so the "Subject to Section 4" blank is traceable in the record.

**No redline was proposed**, which is the required output here — the clause meets the preferred position, and the playbook is explicit that a compliant clause is not redlined.

One judgment call worth surfacing: I considered adding "for convenience" to §14 to satisfy the keyword check directly, but declined and instead logged it as an optional, only-if-already-reopened drafting note. Editing a clause that already sits at preferred purely to match a search pattern would mean reopening a favourable provision for cosmetic gain — the downside risk outweighs the benefit.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
COMPLIANT — the rule is satisfied at the preferred position. No redline is proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

CUSTOMER CONVENIENCE RIGHT IS PRESENT (keyword artifact reconciled). Section 14 (p0079) grants Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional, no-cause right to exit: TrueLink continues the Hosting and Support Services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." The clause expresses the convenience right functionally — "election to terminate," unqualified by any breach, cause, consent or justification requirement — rather than using the label "convenience." A term-search for the word "convenience" therefore returns no hit in Section 14 (the only use of that word in the document is Section 22, p0088, the captions boilerplate), but that is a drafting-vocabulary artifact and not a substantive gap. The operative test under this rule is which party may terminate without cause, on what notice, and at what cost, and Section 14 answers all three in our favour.

MATERIAL TERMS. (1) Notice: the effective notice period runs from ~30 to ~60 days depending on where in the month notice falls, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and comfortably inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. (3) Vendor side is directionally correct: TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right. Its only exits are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical end-of-term non-renewal. (4) Term: a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods (p0078), so the multi-year walk-away trigger ("no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term") does not apply.

SUB-ELEMENTS NOTED, NOT REDLINED. (a) No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — functionally moot because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due within 15 days of receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues to be refunded. (b) The mutual 30-day non-renewal notice is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor exit, but it is an end-of-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience termination, and it is symmetrical — equally available to us — so we would not trade for a longer period. (c) The "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out in Section 14 points to the Support Services minimum commitment at p0043, left blank as "not less than ____ months."

NEGOTIATION FOLLOW-UP (drafting points, no redline under this rule). Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering — termination lives in Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. The Section 4 minimum-commitment blank should be filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since an unfilled or long period could be argued to qualify our Section 14 exit as to Support Services. Optionally, and only if the counterparty is reopening this article for other reasons, we could add the words "for convenience" to Section 14 for clarity; we would not raise it on its own, as the right is already unambiguous and reopening a favourable clause carries more downside than the cosmetic benefit.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right runs against Client anywhere in the Agreement, and TrueLink has no right of access to Client systems for usage verification. This was confirmed by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" — all nil or irrelevant) and by reading the sections where such a right would sit: Compensation (§ 5–6), Client covenants (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information-flow rights point our way: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Because no audit obligation binds us, our position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: proposing audit machinery would only create a vendor right that does not exist today. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is explained by the total absence of an audit clause, not by a permissive one. Noted for awareness only (not a deviation under this rule): § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, but that operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is an acceptable-use enforcement measure, not an audit of our records or systems.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Mortgage Logic.com as Client, and no vendor right of access to our systems for usage verification. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor" and "books" returned no hits, and the two sections the playbook flags as likely homes for such a right contain only customer-favourable provisions:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — the information right runs in *our* favour: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges on request, and we may contest charges (subject to timely payment of contested amounts).
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no examination or verification right. § 2.e in fact gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

Since no audit right binds us at all, our position is stronger than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to constrain and flagging would only invite the counterparty to add a right that does not currently exist.

One item noted for awareness rather than as a deviation: § 8.f permits TrueLink "at any time to implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming. That is an enforcement measure applied to TrueLink's own Interface, not an audit of our records or systems, so it belongs to the acceptable-use analysis rather than this rule.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right runs against Client anywhere in the Agreement, and TrueLink has no right of access to Client systems for usage verification. This was confirmed by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" — all nil or irrelevant) and by reading the sections where such a right would sit: Compensation (§ 5–6), Client covenants (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information-flow rights point our way: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Because no audit obligation binds us, our position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: proposing audit machinery would only create a vendor right that does not exist today. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is explained by the total absence of an audit clause, not by a permissive one. Noted for awareness only (not a deviation under this rule): § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, but that operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is an acceptable-use enforcement measure, not an audit of our records or systems.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

**What I found**
- §2(d) (p0029) is the only ownership provision and runs one way — TrueLink retains all ownership in the Interface (fine in itself; vendor platform ownership is acceptable).
- There is no counterpart clause confirming that Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, Credit Data or other Client data remain ours, and nothing addresses ownership of, or a perpetual licence to, the Support Services results we pay for under §4.
- §10 (p0063, p0065) only makes Client's Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential — a secrecy obligation, not ownership or a licence.
- §13 (p0078) says we retain ownership of domains and Client Content, but only in the discontinued-service context.
- §8(d) (p0054) licenses narrowly defined, aged Credit Data to TrueLink on a non-exclusive basis subject to the Non-Competition Agreement — a licence, not an assignment, so I did not flag it as walk-away.

Neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met on a material term (no Customer Data ownership statement; no ownership of or perpetual, irrevocable licence to work product), so a redline is warranted.

**Proposed redline (validated, ok:true)** — new §2(e) inserted after p0029 reserving our content, IP and data, assigning Support Services work product to us, licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP on a perpetual, royalty-free basis, and excluding joint ownership. Comment offers the fallback (TrueLink keeps generic tools/know-how provided we keep the perpetual licence).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only ownership provision (§2(d)) runs one way: TrueLink retains all rights in the Interface, and nothing in the Agreement affirms that we retain rights in Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property or our borrower/loan data, nor does anything address ownership of the Support Services results we pay for. Section 10 only makes Client's Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential (p0065), which is a secrecy obligation and not an ownership or licence right, and §13's statement that we retain ownership of domains and Client Content applies only on discontinuation of Hosting Services. So neither the preferred position (Customer owns work product, retains all rights in Customer Data) nor the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) is met on a material term. No assignment of our IP or data to TrueLink and no joint ownership is created, so this is not walk-away territory; the §8(d) licence of narrowly defined, aged Credit Data (p0054) is a non-exclusive licence subject to the Non-Competition Agreement and we have not flagged it. Minimal fix: insert a Client ownership subsection at §2(e) reserving our content, IP and data, assigning Support Services work product to us, and licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP.

Original paragraphs:
p0029: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
p0054: d. Use of Credit Data during the term of this Agreement. Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.
p0065: (i) any implementation information or user's guides for the Interface, (ii) any advance releases of TrueLink promotional material, (iii) information concerning TrueLink's business plans and strategies, and (iv) TrueLink's customer list. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will be automatically deemed Client Proprietary Information: Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services, including any information or materials of any type or nature, tangible or intangible, disclosed by Client as a result of the TrueLink's relationship with Client relating to the business, products or technology or potential business, products or technology of Client, business plans, financial information, borrower and loan data technical specifications, design concepts,

Rendered redline:
p0029: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
e. Client Ownership. Client retains all right, title and interest in and to Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, Credit Data and all other data and materials provided by or on behalf of Client or generated through Client's use of the Interface, and nothing in this Agreement operates as an assignment or transfer of any ownership interest therein to TrueLink. All results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared specifically for Client are the property of Client, and TrueLink hereby assigns the same to Client; to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded therein, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense such TrueLink Intellectual Property as part of such results and work product in the ordinary course of Client's business. No intellectual property is jointly owned under this Agreement.

[Playbook] Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's ownership of the Interface but the Agreement never reserves our side, so we have added a matching clause confirming that our content, IP and data remain ours, that results of the Support Services we pay for are ours, and that any TrueLink IP embedded in them is licensed to us on a perpetual, royalty-free basis. If TrueLink prefers, we can accept the fallback of TrueLink retaining its generic tools and know-how so long as we keep that perpetual, worldwide licence to use, modify and sublicense the results.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right runs against Client anywhere in the Agreement, and TrueLink has no right of access to Client systems for usage verification. This was confirmed by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" — all nil or irrelevant) and by reading the sections where such a right would sit: Compensation (§ 5–6), Client covenants (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information-flow rights point our way: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Because no audit obligation binds us, our position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: proposing audit machinery would only create a vendor right that does not exist today. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is explained by the total absence of an audit clause, not by a permissive one. Noted for awareness only (not a deviation under this rule): § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, but that operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is an acceptable-use enforcement measure, not an audit of our records or systems.

input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight to the signature block, so no insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. This is material rather than a drafting nicety because TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives Credit Data consisting of borrower and loan-applicant credit information from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). A vendor that processes personal financial data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, and neither the preferred nor the fallback position (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is met. The gap is also not cured elsewhere: TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b is uncapped-by-insurance and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at 12 months' hosting and support fees, so we have no funded backstop for a data incident. Proposed new Section 31 inserted after § 30 (before the signature block) with the preferred package — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request — using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data). input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight to the signature block, so no insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. This is material rather than a drafting nicety because TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives Credit Data consisting of borrower and loan-applicant credit information from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). A vendor that processes personal financial data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, and neither the preferred nor the fallback position (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is met. The gap is also not cured elsewhere: TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b is uncapped-by-insurance and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at 12 months' hosting and support fees, so we have no funded backstop for a data incident. Proposed new Section 31 inserted after § 30 (before the signature block) with the preferred package — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request — using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data). The fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if TrueLink pushes back on limits.

paragraphs.text: 2. LICENSE.

a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such

software or services do not infringe upon any of TrueLink's Intellectual Property. Nothing in the foregoing sentence is meant to affect in any way Client's confidentiality obligations pursuant to Section 10 herein.
b. Scope. The license granted to Client pursuant to section 2(a) consists of the following rights:
i. Use and execution of the Interface on a compatible software platform (as such compatibility specifications may be issued by TrueLink from time to time); and
ii. Access to the Interface from multiple computer located at those sites listed on Exhibit "A." Client may amend Exhibit "A" by giving TrueLink written notice of the new sites.
c. Term. The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12.
d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
3. HOSTING SERVICES. TrueLink will provide the following services to Client (the "Hosting Services"):
a. Storage. ___ megabytes (MB) of disk space on TrueLink's servers will be used for storage of the Web Site and any data files associated with the Web Site.

b. Response Time. TrueLink agrees to use reasonable commercial efforts, consistent with efforts provided to its other Clients to ensure reasonable response times for users accessing the Web Site. Reasonable response times shall be measured as follows: at a mutually agreed to time Client will conduct three tests of the time that it takes to load the home page of the Web Site from an IBM compatible computer (with a 16550 UART chip and an Intel 80586 300 MHZ processor running Windows 98 or NT and Microsoft Internet Explorer (with the cache turned off) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem (the results of these tests will be reported to TrueLink upon completion); reasonable response times means that at all times the time it takes to load the home page of the Web Site using a properly configured IBM compatible computer (as set forth above) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem shall in no event exceed twice the average of the three test response times.

c. Bandwidth. ___ MB of monthly bandwidth (data transfer). In the event that the response time is not reasonable as determined under section 3.1 hereof, upon written notice from Client, TrueLink will, within a reasonable period of time, use reasonable commercial efforts to increase the bandwidth as necessary to make the response time reasonable.

d. Availability. The Web Site will be available Client's to Internet users approximately 24 hours a day, seven days a week, normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted. To minimize server downtime during peak usage periods,
TrueLink will take all reasonable actions to attempt to schedule routine maintenance between the hours of 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. pacific standard time.
e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.

f. Backups. TrueLink will backup the Interface and all data files associated with it at least once each day and will store the backup materials in a safe, secure location, suitable for magnetic media, and not at
the same location as TrueLink's server.
g. Internet Connection. TrueLink will maintain redundant connections to the Internet on diverse backbones.

h. Domain Names. TrueLink shall provide assistance to Client in securing one or more domain names, sub-domain names or URL's associated therewith; provided that prior to TrueLink providing such assistance, Client shall engage in an appropriate trademark search reasonably satisfactory to TrueLink in order to establish that no domain name proposed by Client shall infringe upon the trademark, service mark, name, or logo of any third party. TrueLink will not be responsible for, or have any liability in connection with, the operation of the Web Site with respect to online commercial transactions, or for the transmission accuracy or completeness of any data or information to or from the Web Site or through the Interface by Client or Client's customers.

i. Credit Bureau Information. TrueLink shall transmit such credit data to Client through the Interface as may be permitted under the Credit Repository Agreements and applicable law, each as in affect from time to tome, and in accordance with the certain Credit Bureau Agreement between TrueLink and Client dated of even date herewith. Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface. TrueLink makes no representation or warranty, and shall have no liability for the truth or completeness of any data so transmitted.

4. SUPPORT SERVICES. For a period of not less than ____ months, TrueLink will make available to Client the services of at least one programmer identified by TrueLink and reasonably acceptable to Client to provide such Support Services as Client may reasonably request to TrueLink in writing for purposes of permitting Client to use the Interface in accordance with the License granted under Section 2 hereof and the other terms and conditions of this Agreement.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

I have what I need. The document does contain termination provisions (mis-numbered inside the "INDEMNITY" section), and they are favorable to us.

**Analysis:**
- **§13 (p0078):** Initial term is **1 year**, auto-renewing in one-year increments, with **symmetrical** 30-day non-renewal notice for either party. Not a multi-year lock-in.
- **§14 (p0079):** Client has an unconditional **termination-for-convenience right on written notice**, effective the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days). No cause required, **no early-termination fee or penalty**.
- **TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right** — its only exit rights are for Client breach (§13(a)-(b), for cause) or symmetrical non-renewal at term end.
- **§5 (p0045):** Fees are invoiced **monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt** (in arrears), so there are no prepaid fees and the pro-rata refund mechanic is functionally moot.

This meets the preferred position on every material term, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale:
The rule is satisfied at the preferred position. Section 14 (p0079) gives Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right exercisable by written notice, with services continuing only until the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, at or better than the preferred 30 days and well inside the 60–90 day fallback. No cause, consent, or justification is required, and no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-fee clawback is imposed anywhere in the agreement.

Direction is also correct on the Vendor side: TrueLink has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term. Its only exit routes are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 upon Client breach or a Credit Repository/System Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical non-renewal at the end of a one-year period. The term is a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in one-year increments (p0078), so there is no multi-year commitment and no walk-away exposure.

input.rationale:
COMPLIANT — the rule is satisfied at the preferred position. No redline is proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

CUSTOMER CONVENIENCE RIGHT IS PRESENT (keyword artifact reconciled). Section 14 (p0079) grants Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional, no-cause right to exit: TrueLink continues the Hosting and Support Services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." The clause expresses the convenience right functionally — "election to terminate," unqualified by any breach, cause, consent or justification requirement — rather than using the label "convenience." A term-search for the word "convenience" therefore returns no hit in Section 14 (the only use of that word in the document is Section 22, p0088, the captions boilerplate), but that is a drafting-vocabulary artifact and not a substantive gap. The operative test under this rule is which party may terminate without cause, on what notice, and at what cost, and Section 14 answers all three in our favour.

MATERIAL TERMS. (1) Notice: the effective notice period runs from ~30 to ~60 days depending on where in the month notice falls, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and comfortably inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering — termination lives in Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. Optionally, and only if the counterparty is reopening this article for other reasons, we could add the words "for convenience" to Section 14 for clarity; we would not raise it on its own, as the right is already unambiguous and reopening a favourable clause carries more downside than the cosmetic benefit.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Mortgage Logic.com as Client, and no vendor right of access to our systems for usage verification. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor" and "books" returned no hits, and the two sections the playbook flags as likely homes for such a right contain only customer-favourable provisions:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — the information right runs in *our* favour: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges on request, and we may contest charges (subject to timely payment of contested amounts).
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no examination or verification right. § 2.e in fact gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

Since no audit right binds us at all, our position is stronger than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to constrain and flagging would only invite the counterparty to add a right that does not currently exist.

One item noted for awareness rather than as a deviation: § 8.f permits TrueLink "at any time to implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming. That is an enforcement measure applied to TrueLink's own Interface, not an audit of our records or systems, so it belongs to the acceptable-use analysis rather than this rule.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right runs against Client anywhere in the Agreement, and TrueLink has no right of access to Client systems for usage verification. This was confirmed by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" — all nil or irrelevant) and by reading the sections where such a right would sit: Compensation (§ 5–6), Client covenants (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information-flow rights point our way: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Because no audit obligation binds us, our position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: proposing audit machinery would only create a vendor right that does not exist today. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is explained by the total absence of an audit clause, not by a permissive one. Noted for awareness only (not a deviation under this rule): § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, but that operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is an acceptable-use enforcement measure, not an audit of our records or systems.

**Finding resubmitted: Compliant — no redline, no comment.**

What I changed in the repair: the finding now cites only the two paragraphs that actually carry evidentiary weight (§ 6 documentation/disputes and § 2.e usage-statistics access, both customer-favourable), dropping § 5.a and § 8.f from the citation list, and the rationale expressly disposes of the failed deterministic check.

Verification performed before resubmitting:

- **Term searches (all nil or irrelevant):** "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "premises", "examination", "certif". "Usage" returns only § 2.34 server-downtime language and § 2.e.
- **Sections read in full:** § 5–6 (Compensation), § 8 (Client covenants and warranties), § 10 (Confidentiality) — the three places a usage or records audit would conventionally sit. None contains an examination, verification or self-certification right, and § 10 contains no inspection or verification mechanic attached to the confidentiality obligations.
- **Rights that do exist run in our favour:** § 6 entitles us to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them; § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

Why compliant rather than missing: AUDIT is a constraining rule — its purpose is to cap frequency, require notice, allocate cost to the vendor and bar system access. With no audit right binding us at all, we sit above the preferred position, so the rule has nothing to constrain. Treating this as "missing" and inserting audit machinery would manufacture a vendor right that does not exist today, which is the opposite of the playbook's intent. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails for absence, not permissiveness.

Carried forward as awareness only: § 8.f permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms against spamming — an acceptable-use enforcement measure on its own Interface, not an audit of our records or systems, so it is not flagged here and is left to the acceptable-use rule.

input.quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
input.rationale: The only TrueLink-side warranty in the Agreement (Section 9, p0059-p0060) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no warranty that the Hosting Services or Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running from TrueLink, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. Section 8 by contrast imposes compliance-with-laws, IP and malicious-code warranties on Client, so the warranty burden is effectively one-directional. Section 12 (p0076) then disclaims all implied warranties of merchantability and fitness "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" - the carve-out is properly worded, but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
input.rationale: The only TrueLink-side warranty in the Agreement (Section 9, p0059-p0060) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no warranty that the Hosting Services or Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running from TrueLink, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. Section 8 by contrast imposes compliance-with-laws, IP and malicious-code warranties on Client, so the warranty burden is effectively one-directional. Section 12 (p0076) then disclaims all implied warranties of merchantability and fitness "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" - the carve-out is properly worded, but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. This fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on a material term, so we insert the express warranty and remedy after p0060 at the preferred period (12 months software, professional and workmanlike services), noting the 90/30-day fallback in the comment.

reasons: The rule is genuinely unmet: §2(d) reserves only TrueLink's rights in the Interface, and nothing in the cited text gives Client ownership of Support Services work product or the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense results — so the clause fails the fallback on a material term and 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The rationale correctly distinguishes the §10 confidentiality treatment of Client's IP and Support Services results (a secrecy obligation, not ownership) and the §13 reservation limited to discontinuation of Hosting Services, and correctly declines to treat the §8(d) non-exclusive Credit Data licence as a walk-away assignment or to double-flag it.

The redline is actionable and tracks the redline guidance with a minimal additive fix: a new §2(e) reserving Client Content/IP/data ownership, assigning Support Services work product to Client, granting a licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, and barring joint ownership; it leaves the counterparty-favourable §2(d) Interface ownership intact and does not disturb the existing §8(d) licence (retained title is compatible with a non-exclusive licence).

The comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the fallback; the deterministic checks (operation applies, no residual assignment of Customer IP/Data to Vendor) are consistent with the substance of the edit.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 10. CONFIDENTIALITY.

a. Client acknowledges its responsibility to preserve the confidentiality of certain technology, information, and documentation embedded in the Interface and agrees to respect the confidential nature of the Interface. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, it is understood and agreed that Client's confidentiality obligations relating to any System and any data, documentation, or other output from such System shall include those specified in any agreements between Client and the licensor of the System.

b. TrueLink acknowledges its responsibilities to preserve the confidentiality of all results of the Support Services, Client's Intellectual Property, and subject to Section 8(d) herein Client Confidential Information.

c. The parties hereto recognize that certain of the information and documentation previously provided or that may in the future be provided by a party to the other related to the matters covered by this Agreement includes privileged, confidential and proprietary information belonging to such party (a party's "Proprietary Information") which, if disclosed, could result in substantial and irreparable harm to such party. For information and documentation to qualify as a party's Proprietary Information, such information must either be marked "Confidential" or otherwise identified in writing as confidential at or prior to the time of its delivery to the other hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will automatically be deemed TrueLink Proprietary Information, whether or not specifically marked or designated as such:

(i) any implementation information or user's guides for the Interface, (ii) any advance releases of TrueLink promotional material, (iii) information concerning TrueLink's business plans and strategies, and (iv) TrueLink's customer list. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will be automatically deemed Client Proprietary Information: Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services, including any information or materials of any type or nature, tangible or intangible, disclosed by Client as a result of the TrueLink's relationship with Client relating to the business, products or technology or potential business, products or technology of Client, business plans, financial information, borrower and loan data technical specifications, design concepts,

-6- 7 technical information, customer lists, pricing information, marketing plans and other similar information pertaining to Client. Each agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials as strictly confidential, except to the extent otherwise agreed by the other in writing. Except to the extent otherwise agreed by both parties in writing, party further agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials which it prepares using or based on the other's Proprietary information or any portion thereof (the "Derivative Documentation") as strictly confidential, including, without limitation, any notes made and all reports prepared in connection with this Agreement.

d. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the restrictions on disclosure and other obligations set forth above with respect to Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation shall not apply when, and to the extent that such Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public through no fault of the receiving party; (ii) was previously known to the receiving party free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iii) is subsequently disclosed to the receiving party by a third party who may transfer and disclose such information without restriction and free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iv) is independently developed by the receiving party or a third party without reference to or any use of the

disclosing party's proprietary information; or (v) is required to be disclosed by the receiving party as a matter of law, provided that the receiving party uses all reasonable efforts to provide the disclosing party with at least ten days' prior notice of such disclosure.

11. STANDARD OF CARE. TrueLink shall perform the Hosting and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services for Client with the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight to the signature block, so no insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. This is material rather than a drafting nicety because TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives Credit Data consisting of borrower and loan-applicant credit information from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, and neither the preferred nor the fallback position (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is met. The gap is not cured elsewhere: TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b is unsupported by any coverage requirement, and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at 12 months' hosting and support fees, so we have no funded backstop for a data incident. Proposed new Section 31 inserted after § 30, before the signature block, with the preferred package — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request — using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data). The fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if TrueLink pushes back on limits.

If helpful we can fall back to E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber liability of USD 2,000,000.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Kind: missing

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
