Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

I have what I need. The document does contain termination provisions (mis-numbered inside the "INDEMNITY" section), and they are favorable to us.

**Analysis:**
- **§13 (p0078):** Initial term is **1 year**, auto-renewing in one-year increments, with **symmetrical** 30-day non-renewal notice for either party. Not a multi-year lock-in.
- **§14 (p0079):** Client has an unconditional **termination-for-convenience right on written notice**, effective the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days). No cause required, **no early-termination fee or penalty**.
- **TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right** — its only exit rights are for Client breach (§13(a)-(b), for cause) or symmetrical non-renewal at term end.
- **§5 (p0045):** Fees are invoiced **monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt** (in arrears), so there are no prepaid fees and the pro-rata refund mechanic is functionally moot.

This meets the preferred position on every material term, so no redline is warranted.

input.rationale:
The rule is satisfied at the preferred position. Section 14 (p0079) gives Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right exercisable by written notice, with services continuing only until the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, at or better than the preferred 30 days and well inside the 60–90 day fallback. No cause, consent, or justification is required, and no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-fee clawback is imposed anywhere in the agreement.

Direction is also correct on the Vendor side: TrueLink has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term. Its only exit routes are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 upon Client breach or a Credit Repository/System Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical non-renewal at the end of a one-year period. The term is a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in one-year increments (p0078), so there is no multi-year commitment and no walk-away exposure.

Two minor sub-elements fall short of the model language but are not material deviations and are not flagged. First, there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is functionally moot because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due within 15 days of receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues to be refunded. Second, the Vendor's end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the fallback's 90 days, but this is a non-renewal of a one-year term rather than a mid-term convenience termination, and the right is symmetrical — it is equally available to us, so we would not trade for a longer period here.

Two drafting notes worth raising in negotiation but not by redline under this rule: Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering (termination lives in Section 14, and Section 12 is the indemnity), and the "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out in Section 14 points to the Support Services minimum commitment period, which is left blank ("not less than ____ months") at p0043. We should ensure that blank is filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since it could otherwise be argued to qualify our convenience right as to Support Services.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only TrueLink-side warranty in the Agreement (Section 9, p0059-p0060) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no warranty that the Hosting Services or Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty running from TrueLink, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. Section 8 by contrast imposes compliance-with-laws, IP and malicious-code warranties on Client, so the warranty burden is effectively one-directional. Section 12 (p0076) then disclaims all implied warranties of merchantability and fitness "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" - the carve-out is properly worded, but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. This fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on a material term, so we insert the express warranty and remedy after p0060 at the preferred period (12 months software, professional and workmanlike services), noting the 90/30-day fallback in the comment.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Mortgage Logic.com as Client, and no vendor right of access to our systems for usage verification. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor" and "books" returned no hits, and the two sections the playbook flags as likely homes for such a right contain only customer-favourable provisions:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — the information right runs in *our* favour: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges on request, and we may contest charges (subject to timely payment of contested amounts).
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no examination or verification right. § 2.e in fact gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

Since no audit right binds us at all, our position is stronger than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to constrain and flagging would only invite the counterparty to add a right that does not currently exist.

One item noted for awareness rather than as a deviation: § 8.f permits TrueLink "at any time to implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming. - compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

I have what I need. The document does contain termination provisions (mis-numbered inside the "INDEMNITY" section), and they are favorable to us.

**Analysis:**
- **§13 (p0078):** Initial term is **1 year**, auto-renewing in one-year increments, with **symmetrical** 30-day non-renewal notice for either party. Not a multi-year lock-in.
- **§14 (p0079):** Client has an unconditional **termination-for-convenience right on written notice**, effective the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days). No cause required, **no early-termination fee or penalty**.
- **TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right** — its only exit rights are for Client breach (§13(a)-(b), for cause) or symmetrical non-renewal at term end.
- **§5 (p0045):** Fees are invoiced **monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt** (in arrears), so there are no prepaid fees and the pro-rata refund mechanic is functionally moot.

This meets the preferred position on every material term, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale:
The rule is satisfied at the preferred position. Section 14 (p0079) gives Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right exercisable by written notice, with services continuing only until the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, at or better than the preferred 30 days and well inside the 60–90 day fallback. No cause, consent, or justification is required, and no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-fee clawback is imposed anywhere in the agreement.

Direction is also correct on the Vendor side: TrueLink has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term. Its only exit routes are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 upon Client breach or a Credit Repository/System Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical non-renewal at the end of a one-year period. The term is a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in one-year increments (p0078), so there is no multi-year commitment and no walk-away exposure.

Two minor sub-elements fall short of the model language but are not material deviations and are not flagged. First, there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is functionally moot because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due within 15 days of receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues to be refunded. Second, the Vendor's end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the fallback's 90 days, but this is a non-renewal of a one-year term rather than a mid-term convenience termination, and the right is symmetrical — it is equally available to us, so we would not trade for a longer period here.

Two drafting notes worth raising in negotiation but not by redline under this rule: Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering (termination lives in Section 14, and Section 12 is the indemnity), and the "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out in Section 14 points to the Support Services minimum commitment period, which is left blank ("not less than ____ months") at p0043. We should ensure that blank is filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since it could otherwise be argued to qualify our convenience right as to Support Services.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale:
COMPLIANT — the rule is satisfied at the preferred position. No redline is proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

CUSTOMER CONVENIENCE RIGHT IS PRESENT (keyword artifact reconciled). Section 14 (p0079) grants Client (Mortgage Logic.com) an unconditional, no-cause right to exit: TrueLink continues the Hosting and Support Services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." The clause expresses the convenience right functionally — "election to terminate," unqualified by any breach, cause, consent or justification requirement — rather than using the label "convenience." A term-search for the word "convenience" therefore returns no hit in Section 14 (the only use of that word in the document is Section 22, p0088, the captions boilerplate), but that is a drafting-vocabulary artifact and not a substantive gap. The operative test under this rule is which party may terminate without cause, on what notice, and at what cost, and Section 14 answers all three in our favour.

MATERIAL TERMS. (1) Notice: the effective notice period runs from ~30 to ~60 days depending on where in the month notice falls, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and comfortably inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. (3) Vendor side is directionally correct: TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right. Its only exits are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository Agreement default (p0078), and symmetrical end-of-term non-renewal. (4) Term: a 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods (p0078), so the multi-year walk-away trigger ("no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term") does not apply.

SUB-ELEMENTS NOTED, NOT REDLINED. (a) No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — functionally moot because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due within 15 days of receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues to be refunded. (b) The mutual 30-day non-renewal notice is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor exit, but it is an end-of-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience termination, and it is symmetrical — equally available to us — so we would not trade for a longer period. (c) The "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out in Section 14 points to the Support Services minimum commitment at p0043, left blank as "not less than ____ months."

NEGOTIATION FOLLOW-UP (drafting points, no redline under this rule). Section 13's cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination is a mis-numbering — termination lives in Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. The Section 4 minimum-commitment blank should be filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since an unfilled or long period could be argued to qualify our Section 14 exit as to Support Services. Optionally, and only if the counterparty is reopening this article for other reasons, we could add the words "for convenience" to Section 14 for clarity; we would not raise it on its own, as the right is already unambiguous and reopening a favourable clause carries more downside than the cosmetic benefit.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Status: missing** — no insurance clause exists anywhere in the Agreement.

**What I found:**
- A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the section outline has no insurance heading.
- The miscellaneous provisions run continuously from § 13 (Term) through § 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight into the signature block, confirming the gap is a genuine omission rather than a clause filed under an unexpected heading.

**Why this is material and not a minor sub-element:**
TrueLink is squarely the kind of vendor the rule targets. It hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads **Client Content** (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives **Credit Data** — raw borrower and loan-applicant creditworthiness data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). That is personal financial data, so zero insurance falls into the rule's walk-away territory, missing both the preferred package and the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).

I also checked whether the gap was cured indirectly, and it is not — if anything the surrounding bargain makes it worse. TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b has no coverage requirement behind it, and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at just 12 months of hosting and support fees. So in a data incident we would have neither a meaningful contractual cap nor an insurer to look to.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** New § 31 inserted after § 30, before the signature block, at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, held through the term plus one year. I drafted it using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data) so the cyber coverage ties explicitly to what TrueLink actually processes. The comment offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a landing zone if TrueLink resists the amounts.

Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) and then straight to the signature block, so no insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. This is material rather than a drafting nicety because TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b), and transmits and archives Credit Data consisting of borrower and loan-applicant credit information from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d). A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, and neither the preferred nor the fallback position (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is met. The gap is not cured elsewhere: TrueLink's indemnity in § 12.b is unsupported by any coverage requirement, and § 12 caps its liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 at 12 months' hosting and support fees, so we have no funded backstop for a data incident. Proposed new Section 31 inserted after § 30, before the signature block, with the preferred package — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request — using the Agreement's own defined terms (Client Content, Credit Data). The fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if TrueLink pushes back on limits.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: There is a minimum commitment on us: Section 5(a) sets a monthly floor ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, and Section 6 makes those minimum monthly fees non-contestable. However, the commitment sits at the playbook fallback rather than in walk-away territory: (i) exposure is confined to the current 12-month term, since Section 13 runs for one year and renews in one-year increments subject to 30 days' notice of non-renewal by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a stand-alone right to terminate at any time on written notice, with services (and therefore the minimum) ending the last day of the month following notice — roughly a 30-60 day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall payment, penalty or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the document, so we pay only monthly minimums for months actually served. Section 2(a) also confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and may source equivalent services elsewhere, so there is no volume cap or exclusivity backing the floor. Two drafting points to note but not redline: the dollar amounts and the Section 4 support period are left blank and should be completed before signature, and Section 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" is a mis-cross-reference (the minimums are in Section 5(a)); Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" should likewise be confirmed as preserving TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right.

input.rationale: There is a minimum commitment on us: Section 5(a) sets a monthly floor ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, and Section 6 makes those minimum monthly fees non-contestable. However, the commitment sits at the playbook fallback rather than in walk-away territory: (i) exposure is confined to the current 12-month term, since Section 13 runs for one year and renews in one-year increments subject to 30 days' notice of non-renewal by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a stand-alone right to terminate at any time on written notice, with services (and therefore the minimum) ending the last day of the month following notice — roughly a 30-60 day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall payment, penalty or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the document, so we pay only monthly minimums for months actually served. Section 2(a) also confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and may source equivalent services elsewhere, so there is no volume cap or exclusivity backing the floor. Two drafting points to note but not redline: the dollar amounts and the Section 4 support period are left blank and should be completed before signature, and Section 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" is a mis-cross-reference (the minimums are in Section 5(a)); Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" should likewise be confirmed as preserving TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right.

**Final finding: Compliant — no redline, no counterparty comment.**

No changes were made on this pass, because the verifier's own reasoning confirms the classification on every material point and identifies no defect to fix. Specifically, it agrees that: (i) there is no audit, inspection or records-examination right running against Client and no vendor access to Client systems; (ii) that absence puts us above the preferred position, so a redline is unwarranted; (iii) "missing" is inapposite for a rule whose purpose is to constrain a vendor-favourable right; and (iv) the failed `audit frequency limited` check is a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause at all.

Evidence supporting the finding:

- **Nil searches:** "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "premises", "examination", "certif". "Usage" surfaces only § 2.34 downtime language and § 2.e.
- **Sections read in full:** § 5–6 (Compensation), § 8 (Client covenants), § 10 (Confidentiality) — the conventional homes for a usage or records audit. None contains a verification, examination or self-certification mechanic.
- **Rights that do exist favour us:** § 6 (documentation for charges plus right to contest) and § 2.e (real-time usage statistics and raw log files).

One caveat worth flagging for the reviewing team rather than the counterparty: the `audit frequency limited` check will continue to fail on this document no matter what a customer-side reviewer does, because it appears to look for frequency-limiting language and cannot distinguish "no audit clause" from "an unlimited audit clause." The only way to make it pass would be to draft a TrueLink audit right and then cap it — a net loss for Mortgage Logic.com. That is a check-tuning issue, not a drafting one.

Carried forward as awareness only: § 8.f permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms against spamming; this operates on its own Interface and belongs to the acceptable-use rule, not this one.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Confirmed compliant on re-review; no repair was required and none is made. The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Client and no access to Client systems for usage verification. This was established by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" - all nil or irrelevant) and by reading every section where such a right would conventionally sit: Compensation (§ 5-6), Client covenants and warranties (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information flows run in our favour: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. With no audit obligation binding us, our position exceeds the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: inserting audit machinery would create a vendor right that does not exist today. "Missing" is inapposite because this rule constrains a vendor-favourable right rather than requiring a protective clause. The failed "audit frequency limited" deterministic check is an artefact of the total absence of an audit clause, not evidence of a permissive one. Awareness only, not a deviation under this rule: § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, which operates on TrueLink's own Interface as an acceptable-use enforcement measure and is not an audit of our records or systems.

**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — no redline proposed.

The document does contain a minimum commitment on us (Section 5(a): fees "not less than $____ per month" for Hosting and Support Services, made non-contestable by Section 6), so the rule is not absent as the planner hint suggested. But it lands on the playbook fallback rather than the walk-away position:

- **Limited to the current 12-month term** — Section 13 runs one year, renewing in one-year increments with a 30-day non-renewal notice available to either party.
- **Exit right** — Section 14 lets us terminate on written notice, with services and the minimum ending the last day of the month following notice (~30–60 days).
- **No penalty** — there is no shortfall, take-or-pay or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the agreement; we pay minimums only for months actually served.
- **No volume cap or exclusivity** — Section 2(a) confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and may source equivalent services elsewhere.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: the fee amounts and the Section 4 support period are blank and should be completed before signature; Section 6's reference to "minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" is a mis-cross-reference (they sit in Section 5(a)); and Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" should be confirmed as preserving TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
There is a minimum commitment on us: Section 5(a) sets a monthly floor ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, and Section 6 makes those minimum monthly fees non-contestable. However, the commitment sits at the playbook fallback rather than in walk-away territory: (i) exposure is confined to the current 12-month term, since Section 13 runs for one year and renews in one-year increments subject to 30 days' notice of non-renewal by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a stand-alone right to terminate at any time on written notice, with services (and therefore the minimum) ending the last day of the month following notice — roughly a 30-60 day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall payment, penalty or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the document, so we pay only monthly minimums for months actually served. Section 2(a) also confirms we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and may source equivalent services elsewhere, so there is no volume cap or exclusivity backing the floor. Two drafting points to note but not redline: the dollar amounts and the Section 4 support period are left blank and should be completed before signature, and Section 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" is a mis-cross-reference (the minimums are in Section 5(a)); Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" should likewise be confirmed as preserving TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right.

**Analysis:**
- **§13 (p0078):** Initial term is **1 year**, auto-renewing in one-year increments, with **symmetrical** 30-day non-renewal notice for either party. Not a multi-year lock-in.
- **§14 (p0079):** Client has an unconditional **termination-for-convenience right on written notice**, effective the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days). No cause required, **no early-termination fee or penalty**.
- **TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right** — its only exit rights are for Client breach (§13(a)-(b), for cause) or symmetrical non-renewal at term end.
- **§5 (p0045):** Fees are invoiced **monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt** (in arrears), so there are no prepaid fees and the pro-rata refund mechanic is functionally moot.

This meets the preferred position on every material term, so no redline is warranted.

**Submitted — status held at compliant.** I'm stopping tool calls here.

**What I repaired this round:** rather than restate the same reasoning a third time, I tested the one hypothesis that could have satisfied the check honestly — that the convenience right might be stated expressly somewhere I hadn't cited. It isn't:

- `convenience` → one hit only, the captions boilerplate at §22 (p0088)
- `without cause` → no hits
- `for any reason at any time` → no hits
- `election to terminate` → p0079 only

**Why I stopped short of making the check pass.** The check is now provably unsatisfiable without inserting "for convenience" into p0079 — editing a clause that already sits at the preferred position. I declined, for two reasons:

1. The playbook is explicit that a clause meeting preferred is not redlined. Flipping to `deviation` to clear a keyword would be over-flagging, and the verifier's own notes say so.
2. Practically, it works against our client. Reopening our single best exit right — no-cause termination, ~30–60 days, zero termination fee — invites TrueLink to counter on notice period or attach a fee, in exchange for a purely cosmetic word change.

So I recorded the check as **requiring reviewer waiver** rather than cure, with the search evidence in the rationale so the next person doesn't repeat the loop. If the house rule genuinely requires the literal word for downstream tooling, that's a drafting-standards decision for a human to take with the commercial risk in view — not something I should resolve by amending favourable text.

Two cleanup items remain logged for negotiation, neither a deviation: §13's mis-cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination, and the unfilled `____ months` Support Services commitment at p0043, which should be set at a figure we're comfortable with so it can't be read to qualify our §14 exit.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
COMPLIANT at the preferred position. No redline and no counterparty comment, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

STATUS OF THE FAILED CHECK — RECOMMEND HUMAN OVERRIDE; NO FURTHER REPAIR AVAILABLE. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" has now failed three times on identical text while every substantive verifier note confirms compliance. I have searched exhaustively for any alternative paragraph that states the right in express terms: "convenience" appears exactly once in the document and it is the captions boilerplate at Section 22 (p0088); "without cause" and "for any reason at any time" return no hits; "election to terminate" returns only p0079. The right therefore has no textual home other than Section 14. The check can only be made to pass by amending p0079 to insert the words "for convenience" — that is, by redlining a clause that already meets the preferred position. I have declined to do so: the playbook is explicit that a clause meeting preferred is not redlined, and reopening a favourable termination provision to satisfy a keyword pattern would expose us to counterparty counter-proposals on our best exit right for purely cosmetic gain. The check should be waived by the reviewer as a phrasing variant, not cured by an edit.

WHY THE CLAUSE MEETS THE RULE. Section 14 (p0079) operationalises a Client "election to terminate this Agreement" that is unqualified by breach, cause, consent or justification — a convenience right expressed functionally rather than by label. (1) Notice: service runs only to the last day of the month following the notice month, an effective ~30–60 days, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. (3) Vendor side: TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit; its only routes out are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository Agreement default (p0078), plus symmetrical end-of-term non-renewal. (4) Term: 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods (p0078), so the "multi-year term with no Customer convenience right" walk-away test is not engaged.

SUB-ELEMENTS NOTED, NOT REDLINED (flagging these would over-flag a clause that benefits us). No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — moot, because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due 15 days after receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues. The mutual 30-day non-renewal notice is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor exit, but it is an end-of-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience right and is symmetrical, so equally available to us. The "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out points to the Support Services minimum commitment at p0043, left blank as "not less than ____ months."

NEGOTIATION FOLLOW-UP (no redline under this rule). Section 13 mis-cross-references "Section 12" for termination when termination is Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. The Section 4 minimum-commitment blank should be filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since an unfilled or long period could be argued to qualify our Section 14 exit as to Support Services. Both are cleanup items to raise if the article is opened for other reasons.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a web site hosting and support agreement under which TrueLink hosts our Web Site, Client Content, backups (Section 2(f)) and borrower/loan Credit Data, so the rule expects an exit clause. None exists. Section 14 only obliges TrueLink to keep providing Hosting and Support Services until the last day of the month following our termination notice — roughly 30-60 days of continued service, not transition or migration assistance. Section 13 (p0078) confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content and gives us 30/60 days to arrange a new name server and hosting environment, but it places that burden entirely on us and imposes no obligation on TrueLink to return, export or delete our data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy provision at all, so even that partial substitute is absent, and searches for return/export/delete/destroy/transition produced no relevant provision. The fallback (90 days' assistance plus data export within 30 days) therefore also fails. Inserted the preferred position into Section 14: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. Placement in Section 14 is effective post-termination because Section 24 (p0090) provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination. We would accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
This is a web site hosting and support agreement under which TrueLink hosts our Web Site, Client Content, backups (Section 2(f)) and borrower/loan Credit Data, so the rule expects an exit clause. None exists. Section 14 only obliges TrueLink to keep providing Hosting and Support Services until the last day of the month following our termination notice — roughly 30-60 days of continued service, not transition or migration assistance. Section 13 (p0078) confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content and gives us 30/60 days to arrange a new name server and hosting environment, but it places that burden entirely on us and imposes no obligation on TrueLink to return, export or delete our data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy provision at all, so even that partial substitute is absent, and searches for return/export/delete/destroy/transition produced no relevant provision. The fallback (90 days' assistance plus data export within 30 days) therefore also fails. Inserted the preferred position into Section 14: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. Placement in Section 14 is effective post-termination because Section 24 (p0090) provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination. We would accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

Original paragraphs:
p0079: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
p0078: 13. TERM OF AGREEMENT. This Agreement will take effect on the Effective Date and remain in effect for a period of 1 year; provided, that Sections 2 and 3 level shall terminate promptly upon (a) any action or omission by Client or any of its customers which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it had pursuant to said Agreements or (b) any violations or breach by Client of Sections 8a - 8c. This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. If Client decides to discontinue its Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new name server within 30 days. In case of discontinued Service, Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content. If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.

Resolved definitions:

("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.
TrueLink: This Agreement is entered into on February 26, 1999, (the "Effective Date") by and between Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. ("Client"), with an address at Two Venture Plaza, 2 Venture, Irvine, California 92618 and TrueLink, Inc. ("TrueLink"), with an address at 3026 South Higuera, San Luis Obispo, California 93401.
Hosting Services: 3. HOSTING SERVICES. TrueLink will provide the following services to Client (the "Hosting Services"):

Rendered redline:
p0079: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable assistance in migrating the Web Site, Client Content and Client's data to Client or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and materials of Client then in TrueLink's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Client Content, Credit Data and other data and materials from its systems and backup media and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added an exit clause requiring TrueLink, on expiry or termination, to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content and Credit Data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and then delete and certify deletion. As TrueLink hosts our Web Site and borrower data, the Agreement currently gives us no right to get that data back or to migrate in an orderly way; we can accept a 90-day assistance period if six months is difficult.

Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity fails even the fallback position, so we added the standard supplier indemnity with the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure. Section 10 only makes Client's Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential (p0065), which is a secrecy obligation and not an ownership or licence right, and §13's statement that we retain ownership of domains and Client Content applies only on discontinuation of Hosting Services. So neither the preferred position (Customer owns work product, retains all rights in Customer Data) nor the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) is met on a material term. No assignment of our IP or data to TrueLink and no joint ownership is created, so this is not walk-away territory; the §8(d) licence of narrowly defined, aged Credit Data (p0054) is a non-exclusive licence subject to the Non-Competition Agreement and we have not flagged it. Minimal fix: insert a Client ownership subsection at §2(e) reserving our content, IP and data, assigning Support Services work product to us, and licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP.","proposal":"Add a Client ownership subsection to Section 2 covering Client Content, Client IP and data, ownership of Support Services results, and a licence back to embedded TrueLink IP.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-6a63cb36","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, buried at the end of the indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting/support compensation, while Client's liability — including the very broad indemnity in Section 12(a) covering any breach, any Client Content claim and product/service injury claims — is entirely uncapped. That is squarely in the rule's walk-away territory ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped"), so it fails the fallback, which requires a mutual 12-month fees cap. The clause is also narrowed to "Section 3, 4, 7 and 11", none of which appear as headings in the document, making even the vendor-side cap of uncertain scope; there is no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere in the Agreement, and no carve-out structure beyond gross negligence/wilful misconduct on TrueLink's side only. Redline makes the cap mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, excludes indirect damages, and places indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; Client's payment obligations are preserved outside the limitation. A straight mutual 12 months' fees cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross negligence carve-outs is the acceptable fallback.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual, extend it to the whole Agreement, add a meaningful floor, exclude indirect damages, and place indemnities/confidentiality outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision (the Section 2 licence grant imposes no separate non-transferability restriction, and the Agreement contains no change-of-control clause, so there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control). The clause is mutual and carves out affiliate assignments, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of our assets would require TrueLink's approval, and the consent standard is unqualified rather than "not unreasonably withheld" — approaching the walk-away position of a prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. The only "exclusive" references run in our favour or are immaterial here: the non-exclusive licence to us (p0022), our grant of a nonexclusive licence in Credit Data to TrueLink (p0054), and an exclusive-forum provision (p0094). Termination (§14) lets Client terminate on written notice with services simply running to the end of the following month — no early-termination fee or minimum-term buyout. No redline and no counterparty comment, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

STATUS OF THE FAILED CHECK — RECOMMEND HUMAN OVERRIDE; NO FURTHER REPAIR AVAILABLE. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" has now failed three times on identical text while every substantive verifier note confirms compliance. I have searched exhaustively for any alternative paragraph that states the right in express terms: "convenience" appears exactly once in the document and it is the captions boilerplate at Section 22 (p0088); "without cause" and "for any reason at any time" return no hits; "election to terminate" returns only p0079. The right therefore has no textual home other than Section 14. The check can only be made to pass by amending p0079 to insert the words "for convenience" — that is, by redlining a clause that already meets the preferred position. I have declined to do so: the playbook is explicit that a clause meeting preferred is not redlined, and reopening a favourable termination provision to satisfy a keyword pattern would expose us to counterparty counter-proposals on our best exit right for purely cosmetic gain. The check should be waived by the reviewer as a phrasing variant, not cured by an edit.

WHY THE CLAUSE MEETS THE RULE. Section 14 (p0079) operationalises a Client "election to terminate this Agreement" that is unqualified by breach, cause, consent or justification — a convenience right expressed functionally rather than by label. (1) Notice: service runs only to the last day of the month following the notice month, an effective ~30–60 days, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. (3) Vendor side: TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit; its only routes out are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository Agreement default (p0078), plus symmetrical end-of-term non-renewal. (4) Term: 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods (p0078), so the "multi-year term with no Customer convenience right" walk-away test is not engaged.

SUB-ELEMENTS NOTED, NOT REDLINED (flagging these would over-flag a clause that benefits us). No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — moot, because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due 15 days after receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues. The mutual 30-day non-renewal notice is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor exit, but it is an end-of-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience right and is symmetrical, so equally available to us. The "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out points to the Support Services minimum commitment at p0043, left blank as "not less than ____ months."

NEGOTIATION FOLLOW-UP (no redline under this rule). Section 13 mis-cross-references "Section 12" for termination when termination is Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. The Section 4 minimum-commitment blank should be filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since an unfilled or long period could be argued to qualify our Section 14 exit as to Support Services. Both are cleanup items to raise if the article is opened for other reasons.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-audit-ddb146fd","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"Confirmed compliant on re-review; no repair was required and none is made. The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Client and no access to Client systems for usage verification. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — findings, walk-away items and next steps

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4. The agreement is workable in structure, and several of our most important commercial freedoms are already protected: the licence is expressly non-exclusive, we are affirmatively free to build or buy competing systems, there is no exclusivity, non-compete, employee non-solicit, MFN or audit right binding us, no liquidated damages or shortfall penalty, and the renewal mechanic (one-year terms, 30 days' non-renewal notice, mutual) and California law/venue both sit within acceptable limits.

The risk is concentrated in the ri[REDACTED] articles, where the document is materially one-sided against us:

- **No Vendor IP indemnity.** Section 12(b) gives us only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink; there is no indemnity anywhere for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents or wilful misconduct, while our indemnity in 12(a) is broad. This fails even the fallback.
- **Asymmetric liability cap.** The only limitation caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting/support compensation while our liability — including the broad 12(a) indemnity — is entirely uncapped. That is expressly walk-away territory under our playbook. There is also no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere, and the vendor-side cap is drafted against "Section 3, 4, 7 and 11", none of which appear as headings, leaving even that cap of uncertain scope.
- **One-way IP ownership.** Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink retains the Interface; nothing affirms that we retain rights in Client Content, our IP or our borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of the Support Services results we pay for.
- **No performance warranty.** The only TrueLink warranty is a Y2K date-processing warranty. Combined with the implied-warranty disclaimer, the practical result approaches an "AS IS" position.
- **No exit clause and no insurance.** There is no transition assistance, data return, export or deletion obligation, and no insurance covenant at all — despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and transmitting and archiving borrower credit data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian.

We have also flagged licence scope (no affiliates or contractors) and assignment (no successor/M&A carve-out, unqualified consent) as high-severity deviations requiring narrow edits.

Three findings carry a failed deterministic check but are substantively compliant on the text (termination for convenience, audit, non-solicit) and are recommended for reviewer waiver rather than redline — editing a clause that already meets our preferred position would only reopen favourable terms.

Separately, the fee blanks (Section 5(a) minimum monthly fee; Section 4 support period) must be completed before signature, and there are two mis-cross-references to clean up (Section 13's reference to "Section 12" for termination; Section 6's reference to minimums "listed in Section 4").

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink; no IP infringement, breach of law, data incident or wilful misconduct indemnity anywhere. Add standard supplier indemnity with notice/control/cooperation procedure. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Ownership runs one way to TrueLink; no reservation of Client Content, Client IP or our data, and no ownership of Support Services results. Add Client ownership subsection at § 2(e) with licence back to embedded TrueLink IP. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink capped at 12 months' compensation; our liability uncapped. No indirect-damages exclusion. Make cap mutual and Agreement-wide, add floor, exclude indirect damages, carve out indemnities/confidentiality/gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud/IP. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 is mutual with an affiliate carve-out but has no successor/M&A carve-out and an unqualified consent standard. Add successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, and bar transfer by TrueLink to a Client competitor. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone; no affiliates or contractors and no notice mechanic to add them. Extend grant to affiliates/contractors and permit transfer to an M&A successor via § 15. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 2(a) expressly confirms we are not obligated to use the licence and may acquire or build similar systems. No redline. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No liquidated damages, penalty or fixed-sum remedy payable by Client; no early-termination fee. Blank minimum monthly fees noted for completion. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us; the referenced Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data. No redline. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Substantively compliant at preferred: § 14 gives an unqualified Client election to terminate, ~30–60 days' run-off, no termination fee, no Vendor convenience exit, 1-year term. Failed keyword check only — recommend reviewer waiver, no edit. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or records-examination right against us anywhere; information flows run in our favour (§ 6 charge documentation, § 2.e usage statistics and logs). Failed check is an artefact of the absence of any audit clause. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law with exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County; sits at the fallback and is accepted. No arbitration provision. Venue convenience noted only. |

| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (waiver recommended) | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No employee non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us — the preferred outcome. Failed checks test fallback wording of a clause that does not exist. Do not volunteer a mutual non-solicit. |

Insert transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days and certified deletion into § 14 (survives under § 24). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only a Y2K warranty from TrueLink; no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no remedy, while § 8 imposes such warranties on us. Add express warranty with repair/replace/refund remedy to § 9. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting Client Content and transmitting/archiving borrower Credit Data. Insert new Section 31 with CGL, E&O and cyber cover plus certificates on request. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They must be resolved before we can recommend signature.

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor liability (§ 12).** Our liability — including the broad 12(a) indemnity covering any breach, any Client Content claim and product/service injury claims — is entirely uncapped, while TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation. This is expressly identified in the rule as walk-away ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped"). The minimum acceptable outcome is a mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnity, confidentiality/data security and gross negligence carve-outs.
2. **No insurance from a vendor processing personal financial data.** TrueLink hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b) and transmits and archives borrower and applicant credit data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d) with no insurance obligation at all. A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance is walk-away territory, and the gap is not cured elsewhere: the § 12.b indemnity is unsupported by any coverage requirement and the vendor-side cap leaves us with no funded backstop for a data incident.
3. **Effective "AS IS" delivery (§ 9 / § 12).** The implied-warranty disclaimer is carved back "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT", but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. We need at minimum the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
4. **Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity.** No indemnity for third-party infringement claims relating to the Interface or the Hosting/Support Services fails even the fallback, leaving us exposed on technology we do not own and cannot control.

---

## Next steps

**Redlines to issue (critical and high, in order of priority)**

1. **§ 12 — Liability.** Make the cap mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000; exclude indirect and consequential damages; place indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; preserve Client payment obligations outside the limitation. Fallback: straight mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross negligence carve-outs.
2. **§ 12 — Indemnity.** Add a TrueLink indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/security incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the usual notice, control and cooperation procedure. We are not narrowing our § 12(a) indemnity in this pass, as it is largely tied to Client Content and our own web site.
3. **§ 2 — Ownership.** Insert a Client ownership subsection at § 2(e) reserving Client Content, Client IP and our data, assigning Support Services work product to us, and licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP. Fallback: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables.
4. **§ 9 — Warranty.** Add an express performance and conformance warranty (12 months software; professional and workmanlike services) with a repair/replace/refund remedy. Fallback: 90 days software / 30 days services.
5. **§ 14 — Exit.** Insert up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and deletion with written certification. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. Placement in § 14 is effective post-termination because § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive.
6. **New § 31 — Insurance.** CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
7. **§ 2 and § 15 — Licence scope and assignment.** Extend the licence to Client affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client assignment, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard on consent, and a bar on TrueLink transferring the Agreement to a Client competitor, preserving the existing mutual structure.

**Reviewer waivers to record (no redline)**

8. Waive the failed deterministic checks on **T4C**, **AUDIT** and **NOSOLICIT** as phrasing variants or artefacts of clause absence. Each is substantively compliant, in each case because the silence or functional drafting favours us, and editing would reopen favourable terms. Under the playbook a clause meeting preferred is not redlined.

**Commercial and drafting cleanup before signature**

9. Complete the **§ 5(a) minimum monthly fee** blank and the **§ 4 support period** blank ("not less than ____ months"), confirming the minimum aligns with the one-month termination runway; an unfilled or long support period could be argued to qualify our § 14 exit as to Support Services.
10. Correct the mis-cross-references: **§ 13** points to "Section 12" for termination when termination is § 14 and § 12 is the indemnity; **§ 6** refers to minimum monthly fees "listed in Section 4" when they sit in § 5(a); and confirm that § 14's "Subject to Section 4" preserves TrueLink's support-availability period rather than qualifying our termination right. Raise if these articles are opened for other reasons.
11. Confirm the scope of the vendor-side cap's reference to "Section 3, 4, 7 and 11", none of which appear as headings in the document.

**Diligence outside this document**

12. Obtain and review the separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at § 8(d). In this document it operates only as a limitation on TrueLink's licensed use of Credit Data, but we should confirm it contains no reciprocal restraint or employee non-solicit binding us.
13. Low-priority ask: raise a **renewal uplift cap** (CPI or 3%) alongside the fee schedule negotiation — § 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year only, leaving renewal uplift uncapped."}

## Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They must be resolved before we can recommend signature.

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor liability (§ 12).** Our liability — including the broad 12(a) indemnity covering any breach, any Client Content claim and product/service injury claims — is entirely uncapped, while TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation. This is expressly identified in the rule as walk-away ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped"). The minimum acceptable outcome is a mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnity, confidentiality/data security and gross negligence carve-outs.
2. **No insurance from a vendor processing personal financial data.** TrueLink hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content (§ 1.b) and transmits and archives borrower and applicant credit data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian (§ 1.d) with no insurance obligation at all. A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance is walk-away territory, and the gap is not cured elsewhere: the § 12.b indemnity is unsupported by any coverage requirement and the vendor-side cap leaves us with no funded backstop for a data incident.
3. **Effective "AS IS" delivery (§ 9 / § 12).** The implied-warranty disclaimer is carved back "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT", but with no express performance warranty to carve out, the practical result approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position. We need at minimum the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
4. **Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity.** No indemnity for third-party infringement claims relating to the Interface or the Hosting/Support Services fails even the fallback, leaving us exposed on technology we do not own and cannot control.
